subject: Onward transfer & full subprocessor roster - request from BankCorp security
messages:
From: Angela Wu <security+vendor@bankcorp.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Ortiz <procurement@bankcorp.com>, BankCorp Legal <dpo@bankcorp.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 08:15:00 -0500
Subject: Request: full subprocessor roster + onward transfer permissions

Karthik —

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of BankCorp's vendor onboarding we need a few items to complete our security review and DPA annexing:

1) A complete, current subprocessor register (vendor name, country, subprocessed data types, purpose, start date).
2) Your policy on subprocessor change notifications (how much notice, opt-out/termination rights).
3) Clarification on onward transfers: do you permit Redwood or any subprocessor to onward-transfer customer data to additional third parties (e.g., specialized analytics partners, managed service partners)? If so, please list categories and whether BankCorp approval is required per transfer.
4) Confirmation that Redwood will enter SCCs (if needed) for EU transfers or otherwise provide equivalent safeguards.

We also need your latest SOC 2 Type II report and SIG/CAIQ if available.

Can you send the subprocessor list and an initial answer on onward transfers by EOD Tuesday (3 business days)? If there are any required contract amendments, please provide a proposed DPA amendment so our legal team can review.

Thanks,
Angela Wu
Senior Vendor Security Analyst
BankCorp Financial Services

--

Folks —

I've prepared an initial subprocessor register and a high-level data flow map. Attaching the CSV and a PDF. Key highlights:

- Infrastructure: Hyperscaler providers (AWS US-EAST-1, GCP-us-central) are used for compute/storage; these are mandatory infrastructure subprocessors for hosted and dedicated offerings.
- Key management: we use an external KMS provider (LocksCo) for our managed KMS option; customers using customer-managed keys keep keys in their account.
- Monitoring & logging: vendor LogSight processes telemetry & aggregated logs for ops; data is pseudonymized for diagnostics.
- Analytics/ML: third-party feature store vendor (FeatureX) is used for non-customer-identifiable model telemetry; we don’t share raw PII.

On onward transfers: Redwood permits onward transfers strictly for the purposes described (infrastructure, security operations, managed services). We do not permit subprocessors to repurpose customer data for their own commercial use. Our practice: customers are notified of new subprocessors with at least 30 days' notice for material changes; in cases where a subprocessor is required to meet critical operations (e.g., new cloud region), we provide expedited notice and customer options in the DPA.

I have included a short summary in the CSV and the data flow map explains where each subprocessor touches data. Legal should weigh in on whether the 30-day notice needs to be formalized as 'prior written consent' or if a 'notice with termination right' model is preferable.

-Vivek
Head of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

--

Attachment: data_flow_map_v1.pdf

Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 10:45:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Request: full subprocessor roster + onward transfer permissions

Angela / BankCorp team —

Thanks for the request and for the patience while we compiled the register. Please find attached a proposed DPA amendment that:

- Inserts an explicit subprocessor register reference (Annex A) and commits Redwood to keep it updated.
- Describes notice for subprocessor changes: Redwood will provide 30 calendar days' notice for new subprocessors; for operationally critical changes (e.g., emergency failover, new cloud region), Redwood will provide as much notice as practicable and document the change; BankCorp will have a right to terminate the Agreement on 30 days' written notice for a material adverse change caused solely by the new subprocessor.
- Onward transfers: the amendment expressly permits onward transfers to third parties strictly for the performance of Redwood's contractual obligations (infrastructure providers, security & monitoring partners, analytics that operate on pseudonymized telemetry). All onward transfers will be subject to either: (a) a contractual flow-down requiring equivalent data protection (SCCs or contractual clauses where applicable), or (b) documented technical controls (e.g., encryption, pseudonymization) and access restrictions.
- SCCs: Redwood confirms willingness to execute SCCs where required for EU transfers.
- We do not transfer customer data for our own marketing or resale.

If BankCorp prefers a model requiring prior written consent for every additional subprocessor, note that could materially slow operations and is atypical for SaaS infrastructure — we propose the 30-day notice + termination right compromise.

Attached: DPA_SCC_amendment_draft_20260228.docx

If this looks acceptable, I can produce a redline suitable for DocuSign and share a link.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

--

Neha / Karthik / Vivek —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and for the detailed register. The DPA amendment draft looks reasonable to our legal team. A couple of quick items before we can finalize:

- Please confirm that LocksCo (KMS) and LogSight (monitoring) are both covered by the proposed flow-down and will be added to Annex A.
- We would like the 30-day notice to trigger a screening period during which BankCorp may provide a termination notice if the subprocessor presents unacceptable risk; the termination would only apply if we exercise that right within 30 days of notice.

If you can confirm the above and provide a DocuSign-ready redline, we can route internally and aim to sign within five business days. If you prefer, share the DocuSign link and we'll initiate the signature workflow.

Appreciate the clarity — this helps keep our compliance program on track.

Regards,
Angela Wu
Senior Vendor Security Analyst
BankCorp Financial Services
